scope: Pre-layout evidence review; no circuit edits; recommendations are not all confirmed failures

findings.title: Rebuild J3 signal lands before PCB release
findings.observed: The current GX.pretty/J3_Recovered.kicad_mod retains 30 signal lands of 0.127 by 1.1176 mm centered at Y=+/-0.7468 mm. Hirose recommends 0.18+/-0.02 mm width, with 1.80/1.18 mm outer/inner row extents, implying 0.31 mm pad length. The recovered lands extend into the central area marked no conductive trace.
findings.consequence: This is a manufacturing geometry defect, not an ERC error. Fine-pitch soldering and connector fit cannot be released with these lands.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild copper, mask, and paste from the exact Hirose drawing; independently verify pin-1/mating orientation. Keep the four end power contacts 31-34 on GND. Obtain a controlled drawing or vendor acceptance for production because the archived sheet is marked reference.

evidence.section: Recommended PCB layout and metal mask

findings.closure: Compare every land and mask aperture numerically, then inspect a 1:1 plot and actual mating part before routing/fabrication.

findings.title: Boot NOR chip select is on the wrong ROM pin
findings.observed: BOOT_XSPI_NCS connects U1 P14/PN12 to NOR /CS. PN12 AF9 is XSPIM_P2_NCS2. U1 R17/PN1 is unused. Other boot pins are PN6 CLK and PN2/PN3 IO0/IO1.
findings.consequence: STM32N6 ROM uses a fixed PN1 AF9 chip select for serial NOR; the selected flash is not addressed by the ROM. Firmware in that flash cannot repair the pin selection before it has booted.
findings.recommended_fix: Move BOOT_XSPI_NCS and its pull-up to U1 R17/PN1, AF9 XSPIM_P2_NCS1. Keep PN6/PN2/PN3; PN4/PN5 may serve quad data after the FSBL. Recheck pin-map and cold boot with a minimal signed/headered FSBL.

evidence.detail: Sections 3.4.5-3.4.6, Table 27: fixed legacy SPI boot on PN6/PN1/PN2/PN3.
VFBGA264 ball map and Table 20: PN1=NCS1; PN12=NCS2 at AF9.

findings.title: Main and auxiliary MCU supplies cannot perform the mandatory sequence
findings.observed: The single 1V8 net joins F6/VDDA18AON to VDDSMPS, VDDA18PMU, VDDA18ADC, VDDA18CSI, VDDA18USB and other domains. U7 EN is tied directly to 3V3. USB-derived 3V3_USB is generated independently from VBUS. PWR_ON only drives the battery latch.
findings.consequence: AN5967 requires main VDD and VDDA18AON first, then auxiliary domains after PWR_ON rises. On shutdown auxiliary rails must discharge below 0.6 V while main supplies remain in their operating ranges. Tying AON to the auxiliary 1.8 V consumers prevents that independent sequence. USB-derived auxiliary power can also precede the main group. A successful bench startup would not establish compliance across corners.
findings.recommended_fix: Separate the main 1.8 V AON domain from auxiliary domains and implement PWR_ON-controlled auxiliary enables with defined discharge and ordering on both battery and USB. Observe permitted exceptions for IO supplies tied to VDD and PLL tied to AON. Capture every rail and PWR_ON during cold start, shutdown, hot plug, brownout and rapid retry before release. Coordinate the latch fixes in power-review.md.

evidence.detail: Section 3.5 and Figures2/3: mandatory main/AUX startup and shutdown sequence; AUX below 0.6 V before main shutdown.
Power-on control and PWR_CR1 POPL/MODE_PDN/SDEN behavior.

findings.title: Battery latch pull-down back-drives the MCU shutter input
findings.observed: D3 anode is LATCH_PULLDOWN and cathode is SHUTTER_SENSE at U1 F3/PC13. When SW1 and Q2 are open, the path common PFET source -> R1 1 MOhm -> R2 100 kOhm -> D3 remains connected to PC13. There is no voltage translation or independent low-voltage switch contact.

evidence.detail: SHUTTER_SENSE contains only PC13, D3 cathode and SW1.1; LATCH_PULLDOWN contains R2, Q2 drain and D3 anode.
PC13 is a TT input; Table 21 limits TT input voltage to 3.6 V in the 3.3 V range.
AO3401A threshold magnitude 0.5-1.5 V, on-resistance specified at VGS=-2.5 V.

findings.consequence: Full PFET turn-off would raise SHUTTER_SENSE toward the 8-13.2 V battery source, beyond PC13 rating. If input structures clamp near the powered 3.3 V domain, current through R1 instead sustains several volts of negative VGS and can keep the battery switch on. The exact clamp/injection waveform needs measurement, but the circuit cannot both turn fully off and keep PC13 within its allowed voltage range.
findings.recommendation: Separate battery-level latch actuation from MCU shutter sensing using an isolated second contact or a properly rated transistor/level-shift circuit. Verify powered-off, boot, release, repeated press and shutdown states before layout; an MCU pull-up or series resistor alone does not remove this latch interaction.

findings.title: Four-CR2032 supply is unqualified for the stated system pulse power
findings.observed: The source specifies four series CR2032 cells, 8-13.2 V, and a provisional 3.3 V peak load of 1.2 A. No production battery MPN or measured boot/capture/save current waveform is provided. The main reservoir is only 4x47 uF plus C3=22 uF nominal.

evidence.detail: U2 Role Details contains the 1.2 A provisional peak budget; capacitors are per-instance 22 uF and 47 uF values.
Unselected reference candidate: 235 mAh rating at 15 kOhm; published pulse test is approximately 6.8 mA for 2 seconds. These are typical reference conditions, not a universal maximum-current rating.
Input/output capacitor selection and DC-bias reduction must be evaluated.

findings.consequence: At the provisional peak, each cell must carry roughly 333-550 mA before source sag. The 210 uF bank supports only about 50 microseconds between 3.3 and 3.0 V. Series cells multiply both voltage and resistance; the architecture cannot be qualified by the mAh number. This does not prove every CR2032 fails at the actual workload; that workload remains unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Before fixing battery mechanics or power routing, select a cell and measure boot, capture and complete NAND-save current over state of charge and temperature with realistic contacts. Replay that waveform on the cell stack and record rail minima and energy. If the source cannot sustain it, change battery chemistry/form factor, lower actual power, or design a deliberately charged energy reservoir with an honest startup-latency budget.

findings.title: NAND ready/busy is routed to FMC_NWAIT instead of FMC_RNB
findings.observed: NAND_RNB is on PF2/N4, whose AF12 is FMC_NWAIT. The actual dedicated FMC_RNB is available on unused PA7/R12 AF12 (also PE4/D10, but that pin uses the 1.8 V bank).
findings.consequence: The N6 NAND controller uses its dedicated RNB input for automatic busy waits, sequencer tWB handling and ready/busy interrupts. FMC_NWAIT is not the same input. Software GPIO/status polling can be a separately validated fallback, but the intended hardware wait/sequencer path is unavailable as wired.
findings.recommended_fix: Move NAND_RNB to PA7/R12 AF12 FMC_RNB on the 3.3 V VDD bank. Retain a suitable 3.3 V pull-up and configure NAND wait timing. Do not substitute PE4 without revisiting voltage compatibility.

evidence.detail: PA7 supports FMC_RNB AF12; PF2 supports FMC_NWAIT AF12.
Table 185 and NAND control description distinguish RNB and its wait/interrupt uses.

findings.title: RTC interrupt pull-up exceeds the receiving bank operating limit
findings.observed: RTC_INT_N at U1 E7/PH2 is pulled to 3V3 by R24. PH2 belongs to VDDIO4, which is supplied by1V8.
findings.consequence: DS14791 Table 24 recommends input voltage at most the receiving supply+0.3 V in the 1.8 V range (about 2.1 V here).3.3 V violates that operating limit. In default VRSEL=0 the TT absolute maximum is 3.6 V, so immediate damage is not proven; after selecting 1.8 V VRSEL=1 its absolute maximum is 1.98 V, making this also an overstress path.
findings.recommended_fix: Pull RTC_INT_N up to 1V8, using the RTC open-drain output, or relocate it to a 3.3 V bank. Verify backup-only isolation and the revised supply order. Do not enable IO4 high-speed 1.8 V mode while this 3.3 V pull-up remains.

evidence.detail: PH2 bank note 6; Table 21 TT absolute limits; Table 24 VIN operating limit.
PWR_SVMCR1 VDDIO4VRSEL and supply-valid controls.

findings.title: NRST capacitor is ten times the specified maximum
findings.observed: C38 is recorded as 100 nF in the native per-instance Capacitance field and connected from NRST to GND.
findings.consequence: DS14791 Table 71 specifies CEXT maximum 10 nF. The existing load is outside the reset-pin characterization and can compromise internally generated or external reset pulses.
findings.recommended_fix: Use C38 no greater than 10 nF, including its positive tolerance, and verify NRST low level and pulse timing with the selected debugger and switch. Apply the silicon-revision reset workaround where needed.

evidence.detail: Section 5.3.18, Table 71 and Figure 25: CEXT maximum 10 nF; VIL maximum 0.65 V.
Section2.2.18: incorrect NRST reset behavior on affected revisions.

findings.title: Library load validation is not footprint manufacturing validation
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / confirmed gap.** All147 host footprints load and cover all703 expected physical host pins. That checks identity/connectivity, not pad geometry, solder mask, paste, courtyard, height or assembly orientation. The camera review identifies a specific J3 geometry problem. Generic L1–L3 and high-value MLCC packages cannot be released until exact MPNs are selected.

**Recommendation:** Rebuild/correct J3 from the manufacturer drawing, select the power passives, and perform a drawing-to-footprint review of every distinct production land pattern. Include exposed pads, paste segmentation, mask web capability, pin1 marks and rotations in assembly outputs. Validate the selected 0.2 mm finished through-hole process and assembly stencil with the vendors. First-article inspection should include BGA X-ray and microscope inspection of J3/USB solder joints. A separate [spot-check report](footprint-spot-check.md) records the critical dimensions actually checked; it is not an all-footprint release certificate. [Existing validation scope](../../hardware/reconstruction/footprint-load-validation.md).

findings.title: PFET gate divider has no absolute-maximum margin at fresh-cell voltage
findings.observed: At Q2 pull-down near 0 V, R1=1 MOhm and R2=100 kOhm set |VGS|=Vsource*R1/(R1+R2). At 13.2 V this is exactly 12.0 V; R1/R2 tolerances are unselected.

evidence.detail: Common-source PFET pair shares the gate divider; native Role Details explicitly uses the 13.2 V fresh stack bound.
HUASHUO AO3401A absolute maximum VGS is +/-12 V, not +/-20 V.

findings.consequence: Ordinary resistor variation can exceed the gate-oxide absolute maximum even without a transient. Equality to an absolute maximum is not an operating-margin design.
findings.recommendation: Provide substantial gate-voltage margin. For example, R2=330 kOhm with R1=1 MOhm and 1% tolerances gives a DC worst case below 10 V at 13.2 V and about 6 V drive at an 8 V source. Alternatively choose an appropriately rated PFET/clamp scheme. Recheck source/gate transients and clamp leakage at the actual microampere bias; the example divider is a proposal, not an applied edit.

findings.title: USB startup automatically reconnects the battery stack
findings.observed: U1 E2/PWR_ON directly drives Q2, which enables the common-gate PFET pair. PWR_ON automatically asserts during normal startup, including startup powered through USB. No VBUS-qualified inhibit exists in the battery hold path.

evidence.detail: PWR_HOLD has only PWR_ON, Q2 gate and R3. D2 anode USB_VBUS, cathode SYS_IN.
PWR_ON is the core/secondary-supply enable and asserts before firmware execution.
PWR_ON uses the VDD domain; VDD is 3.3 V in this design.

findings.consequence: With a normal 8-13.2 V stack present, the battery raises SYS_IN above USB voltage and reverse-biases D2, so USB download can drain the coin cells. Both conducting PFET channels are bidirectional; if stack voltage is below USB-powered SYS_IN, off-state reverse isolation no longer prevents current into the stack. Normal cells should not reach that condition, but no hardware inhibit enforces it.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit USB-priority source selection and battery reverse-current control independent of PWR_ON. Coordinate this with the redesigned latch and mandatory MCU main/auxiliary sequencing. Keep the battery path disabled during USB-only download unless its use is intentionally requested.

findings.title: Power magnetics and MLCC footprints are placeholders without production limits
findings.observed: All three power inductors use generic 0603/1608 footprints and no MPN. L1 is 2.2 uH/4 A target, L2 0.47 uH/3 A target, L3 1 uH/2 A target. No DCR, RMS-current, inductance-vs-bias or actual body dimensions are specified. High-value MLCCs, including C1 10 uF/25 V 0603 and C4-C7 47 uF/6.3 V 0603, also lack MPN, dielectric/tolerance and DC-bias curves.

evidence.detail: Native per-instance component specifications and generated package choices.
Example 2.2 uH inductor is about 4x4 mm; 10 uF/25 V example input capacitor is 1210. These examples do not prohibit smaller qualified parts but show why generic footprints are not a selection.
Requires at least 3 uF effective input and 10 uF effective output; inductor selection includes saturation, DCR and size.

findings.consequence: The schematic values alone do not guarantee stability, current capability, stored energy or footprints that fit an orderable part. A 10 uF nominal MLCC does not establish a 10 uF effective-at-bias target.
findings.recommendation: Select exact production magnetics and MLCCs before placement, verify effective L/C, RMS/saturation current and loss over the operating range, then replace generic footprints with manufacturer land patterns. Verify U2 LC transient response around its roughly 210 uF reservoir and downstream load. Do not claim the existing 0603 parts are impossible; they are presently unqualified.

findings.title: MCU SMPS passive targets and local input bypass do not match the current reference requirements
findings.observed: L3 is specified only for 2 A saturation and has no DCR limit. No dedicated VDDSMPS 2x1 uF plus 2x100 nF input bypass is identified; C10/C11 are allocated to the U7 output, and other 1 uF capacitors have VREF, camera or load-switch roles. The core bulk bank is 4x22 uF, while current ST references specify 4x15 uF typical and an output-impedance range.

evidence.detail: Per-instance values/roles, with all VDDSMPS balls connected to 1V8.
Rev5 Table6 calls for L=1 uH +/-20%, Isat>3 A, DCR<60 mOhm; VDDSMPS bypass 2x10 uF+2x1 uF+2x100 nF; VLX damping 2.2 nF +2 Ohm and four 15 uF output capacitors.
Table27 external coil1 uH, Cout4x15 uF typical and output impedance16-33 mOhm; internal SMPS supports up to2.2 A.

findings.consequence: A part satisfying the existing 2 A target alone need not support the internal converter. Global 1V8 capacitance does not prove the required low-inductance SMPS input bypass. The 88 uF output bank is a deviation to validate, not a proven instability or overvoltage defect.
findings.recommendation: Raise the L3 procurement requirements to the current ST limits and choose a qualified footprint. Allocate the complete local VDDSMPS bank; if sharing U7 output capacitors, justify placement/loop inductance and still supply the required local small capacitors. Select output MLCCs to meet ST impedance/transient requirements; check whether four15 uF or the existing88 uF bank is appropriate. Retain the correctly connected 2 Ohm/2.2 nF snubber and separate V08CAP capacitor.

findings.title: Sensor revision can make a 50 ms cold capture impossible
findings.observed: The module BOM does not identify the sensor silicon cut. Official ST driver revision 0x1111 uses cut1_patch=6868 bytes; revision 0x1120 uses cut2_patch=260 bytes, loaded at each power-on. UM2829 describes the patch load/activation before BOOT and STREAMING.
findings.consequence: At the sensor maximum 1 MHz I2C rate, patch data plus ACK alone takes at least 61.812 ms for cut1 or 2.340 ms for cut2. At 400 kHz those bounds are 154.530 and 5.850 ms. The cut1 path already exceeds 50 ms before power ramp, MCU boot, configuration, exposure, or readout. These are transfer lower bounds, not measured startup times.
findings.recommendation: Read and record the module revision on samples and qualify the production supply to a supported cut/patch combination. Use the approved patch for that cut and measure it; do not omit a required patch merely to meet latency. If only cut1 is available, revise latency or power-retention architecture.
findings.closure: A procurement-controlled sensor revision and measured cold boot-to-valid-frame trace within the allocated budget.

findings.title: Power-down must remove analog power before camera core and I/O
findings.observed: U9 analog enable is controllable, but U10 core enable follows 1V8 and camera I/O is directly on 1V8. The recorded flow ends by releasing the main latch. DS13170 requires XSHUTDOWN low before analog power-down, analog below 20% of its minimum (0.54 V), then at least 1000 us before core/I/O fall. TLV700 has no specified active output-discharge function or guaranteed discharge interval.
findings.consequence: Simultaneously dropping the main latch does not guarantee the required sequence. Disabling U9 and waiting a nominal 1 ms also does not establish that its output capacitor has already discharged below 0.54 V.
findings.recommendation: Stop streaming, enter standby, assert shutdown, disable U9, and keep the upstream/core/I/O rails alive until measured or guaranteed analog decay plus 1 ms has elapsed. Add a defined discharge path or choose a regulator with specified output discharge if software timing cannot bound it. Preserve the existing startup delay of >=1 ms after both lower rails are actually valid before enabling analog.
findings.closure: Scope simultaneous VANA/VCORE/VDDIO/XSHUTDOWN at cold start, normal shutdown, rapid re-press and USB transitions; determine behavior on uncontrolled brownout separately.

findings.title: Shutdown and bank setup need an N6-specific early firmware contract
findings.observed: PWR_HOLD uses dedicated PWR_ON, while the camera/control interfaces use independent 1.8 V banks and the boot flash uses VDDIO3. Firmware is not yet in the repository.
findings.consequence: PWR_ON is a hardware-controlled VDD output, not a writable GPIO: it asserts after main POR and drops in Standby. Firmware that attempts to clear an ordinary GPIO will not release this latch. IO supply-valid controls, voltage-range settings and current errata also affect whether MCLK/control pins work and whether output duty cycles meet specification.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement shutdown by saving/isolating external devices then entering the appropriate Standby sequence; program a sufficient POPL minimum low interval and required discharge, retaining BSECEN. Validate VDDIO3/4/5 supplies before enabling them; select correct voltage modes and OTP HSLV settings only for the corresponding physical voltage. Apply ES0620 fixed I/O-compensation workaround and coupled supply-valid access requirements. Do not fuse OTP until the final supply plan is reconciled.

evidence.detail: PWR_ON powered by VDD; independent-bank voltage selection follows actual bank supplies.
PWR_ON in Standby; POPL default no guaranteed low time; MODE_PDN defaults off; supply-valid and VRSEL controls.
Sections2.2.2,2.2.19,2.2.20: BSECEN requirement and fixed compensation0x287 workaround.

findings.title: Use BCH4 or stronger and protect metadata outside the FMC BCH data path
findings.observed: MX30LF2G18AC requires 4-bit correction per (512+16) bytes. STM32N6 FMC supports BCH4/BCH8 per 512-byte data sector; BCH4 produces 7 parity bytes, or 28 bytes per 2 KiB page. Hamming is the reset/default algorithm and is insufficient. RM0486 explicitly says its BCH encoder does not process spare-area metadata.
findings.consequence: There is no inherent controller ECC-strength incompatibility, but selecting Hamming or putting unprotected commit/allocation data into OOB would leave the required integrity contract incomplete. CRC detects errors but does not replace correction.
findings.recommendation: Configure BCH explicitly, specify an OOB layout retaining factory bad-block markers, and place critical metadata in BCH-protected data sectors or provide its own adequate error protection/redundancy. Flip corrected bits using FMC error locations and handle uncorrectable sectors, erased pages and ECC-field errors.
findings.closure: Documented format plus injected 1-4 bit errors in each data sector, parity and metadata; correctable recovery and deterministic rejection of uncorrectable records.

findings.title: Power-fail recovery must respect partial-program and erase rules
findings.observed: The spec calls for a verified commit and redundant metadata but implementation is not present here. AC permits at most four partial programs per page and requires ascending page order within a block. Macronix warns an interrupted program/erase can appear readable yet have inadequate retention margin. Pulling WP# low or issuing reset during program/erase aborts it.
findings.consequence: A last-minute WP# assertion, a same-page commit-bit rewrite, or an immediate successful readback cannot by itself prove a durable transaction. Reusing an uncertain erased page/block can damage later recovery.
findings.recommendation: Use append-only, BCH-protected commit records and an interrupted-operation ledger; keep old committed records until new ones pass status/ECC/CRC checks. Quarantine/re-erase uncertain blocks. Preserve factory bad-block marks before erase and budget partial-program count including ECC/OOB writes. Keep WP# high until the final operation completes; only then protect and remove power.
findings.closure: Randomly interrupt power throughout data, ECC, commit and erase stages; every reboot must recover prior valid images and reject uncertain new records without erasing valid factory markers.

findings.title: The four-layer target needs a real stackup and an escape trial
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / conditional.** The provisional dielectric values 0.18+1.17+0.18 mm and four 35 µm copper layers sum to 1.67 mm before other finish allowances, rather than the stated 1.6 mm. A nominal Dk and trace width do not specify controlled impedance. The 0.8 mm BGA pitch is compatible with investigating ordinary through-via escape; it does not by itself prove the complete pinout can escape on this board.

For the inherited U1 pad diameter0.394 mm and proposed 0.50 mm via land, a via centered between four balls has nominal copper gap `0.8/sqrt(2) - (0.394+0.50)/2 = 0.1187 mm`. That is only 18.7 µm above the proposed 0.10 mm clearance. A 0.10 mm trace between two 0.50 mm vias on 0.8 mm pitch leaves exactly 0.10 mm on each side. These are ideal geometry calculations, not toleranced manufacturing acceptance. Hole registration, finished hole, annular ring, mask webs and the actual fanout must be checked with the fabricator.

**Recommendation:** Retain four layers as a working cost target. Select a representative fabricator stackup and complete the MCU power/ground, boot bus, NAND and CSI escape before committing placement. If that consumes all routing access or forces poor return paths, compare a conventional six-layer option before adding HDI complexity. Record actual laminate thicknesses, copper weight, mask, impedance tolerance, finished drill and annular-ring rules. [Recovered board rules](../../imports/flux/2026-09-05/recovered-context.md), [U1 package/PCB recommendations](../../datasheets/processor/STM32N657X0_DS14791_datasheet.pdf).

findings.title: High-speed and power routing rules are not yet implemented or verified
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / conditional.** USB and CSI need their intended 90 Ω and 100 Ω differential impedances using the selected stack. FMC and XSPI single-ended edges, camera MCLK, oscillator loops and the internal/external switchers also matter. The Flux failure is not evidence that a general autorouter can solve the power loops, return paths and component dependencies automatically.

**Recommendation:** Place camera connector and MCU CSI side first, with grounded reference continuity; then place each SMPS's input loop, inductor, output bank and Kelvin feedback before ordinary signal routing. Keep L2 continuous under L1 high-speed signals. On other signal layers, explicitly identify the adjacent return plane and avoid crossing power splits. Add nearby ground stitching at layer transitions. Keep CSI pair polarity and lane mapping intact; set pair skew and clock/data constraints from the selected operating mode, including package and flex contribution. Avoid unnecessary vias and long test stubs. Do not add arbitrary series resistors or discrete termination to CSI; its receiver termination is part of the PHY. Route NAND/XSPI with deliberately chosen drive strength and setup/hold margins. [AN5967](../../datasheets/processor/STM32N6_AN5967_hardware_design.pdf), [AN5050](../../datasheets/processor/STM32_AN5050_XSPI_memory_interface.pdf), [module integration manual](../../datasheets/camera/VD55G0_UM2829_integration_registers.pdf).

findings.title: The five-millimetre envelope and camera alignment are not closed
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / conditional.** A 3.2 mm CR2032 above a 1.6 mm PCB already consumes 4.8 mm before contacts, insulation, covers or parts on the opposite face. Four 20 mm cells occupy approximately 1,257 mm² in circular area, around 27% of the 85.6×53.98 mm board; a simple two-by-two bounding rectangle occupies 1,600 mm². The native camera model reference was for a related module, so it is not evidence of the exact lens height or image orientation.

**Recommendation:** Close a sectioned mechanical model with the exact camera STEP, battery contacts, USB overhang, shutter actuator, screw bosses and covers before placing the dense electronics. Compare recessed contacts/cutouts against a modest increase in thickness. Verify flex bend radius, connector mating height, optical aperture, lens protrusion and assembly access. Keep battery cans/contacts insulated by durable mechanical features, and support the thin board to control flex at the BGA and camera connector. The battery and camera envelope can dominate layout more than the nominal PCB outline. [CR2032 reference dimensions](https://data.energizer.com/pdfs/cr2032_eu.pdf), [camera document/STEP record](../../datasheets/camera/README.md), [project requirements](../../spec.md).

findings.title: Backup mode must be provisioned persistently; default is disabled
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / conditional.** U8 has a suitable single-cell backup connection and local bypass, but the RV-3028 is delivered with backup switching disabled. The specification's intended LSM setting is sensible when the 3.3 V main rail and fresh backup cell are close in voltage; it must actually be programmed into EEPROM and verified. A RAM-only setting can be replaced by an EEPROM refresh. In backup-only insertion standby, the clock is not established merely by connecting the cell before the first valid main-power initialization.

**Recommendation:** Define a factory provisioning operation on stable power: set the correct time, persist BSM=11, keep FEDE=1, verify the EEPROM and retention after main power removal, and record a validity flag. Test primary-cell replacement and cold/weak-cell switchover. LSM requires the backup input to exceed its approximately 2 V threshold, so the lowest series cell and sag matter separately from total pack voltage. Changing from disabled to LSM can take 15.625 ms; do not repeat that initialization on every capture. The approximately 66 ms POR refresh applies after true RTC power loss, not each ordinary main-rail cycle with valid backup. [RV-3028 application manual, pp39,43–48,54–57,87](../../datasheets/sensors_timing/RV-3028-C8_application_manual.pdf).

findings.title: The primary backup cell must never have trickle charging enabled
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / conditional.** U8 VBACKUP is directly connected to a non-rechargeable CR2032 tap. EEPROM register37h contains the charger-enable bit alongside backup-mode configuration. TCE defaults off, so an existing enabled charger is not alleged; a careless whole-register write could enable a real charging path from VDD.

**Recommendation:** Keep TCE=0 explicitly, preserve it during all configuration updates, and read back the persistent setting in production. Preserve the factory calibration bit7 in register37h and disable unused CLKOUT in register35h. Include this in the hardware/firmware contract. The manufacturer primary-battery application example uses charging disabled. [RV-3028 application manual, pp39,48,104](../../datasheets/sensors_timing/RV-3028-C8_application_manual.pdf).

findings.title: Attach/detach detection and USB power policy are incomplete
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / conditional.** J1 VBUS feeds U4 and D2, but no explicit VBUS divider/comparator or CC advertisement detector reaches the MCU. The STM32N6 OTGPHY1 has no connection to VBUS; its legacy VBUS/SESSION signals cannot be used as though it had one. The present VBUS-only 3V3_USB supply may permit a qualified supply-status proxy using USB33RDY, but that is not a demonstrated attach/detach implementation. In particular, unplugging USB while batteries keep the MCU powered must remove USB signaling and isolate the PHY correctly.

**Recommendation:** Add explicit, safely scaled VBUS detection, or demonstrate the supply-status approach over threshold, timing, power-order and firmware failure cases. An ADC divider must suit a 1.8 V input and remain safe with its receiving supply off. Coordinate with MCU-002 supply sequencing. USB33VMEN/USB33RDY monitoring supports EXTI edge interrupts, so a validated supply proxy is a real option rather than an assumed unavailable capability. [RM0486 Rev4, §72.2.6 p3751, §72.4.2/Figure978 p3756, supply monitoring pp365,396](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0486-stm32n647657xx-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf#page=3756). ST explicitly requires VBUS sensing for self-powered operation; its GPIO detector examples must be adapted to the N6 input voltage and off-state limits. [AN4879 Rev12, §2.6 pp11–12](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/an4879-introduction-to-usb-hardware-and-pcb-guidelines-using-stm32-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf#page=11).

R10/R11 are correctly separate 5.1 kΩ sink resistors. They advertise a sink; they do not entitle the board to draw 1.5 A or 3 A. Establish a startup, configured and suspend load budget. Remain within default USB power rules unless the advertised current is detected and used correctly. If download mode needs more power, use a suitable CC detector/controller and a source-selection circuit. A selected USB-C source can advertise higher current without USB PD, but the sink has to determine that advertisement. [USB Type-C specification §2.3.4](https://www.usb.org/sites/default/files/USB%20Type-C%20Spec%20R2.0%20-%20August%202019.pdf).

USB descriptors and reported bus/self-powered state must follow the actual source and load. USB-IF's suspend-current update specifies 2.5 mA. Qualify both full-speed fallback and high-speed operation. The separate PWR-003 finding explains why this design currently reconnects its batteries during a USB session. [USB-IF electrical compliance updates](https://compliance.usb.org/index.asp?UpdateFile=Electrical).

findings.title: Define exposure completion and first valid frame for the 50 ms requirement
findings.observed: The specification requires full native resolution and bit depth within 50 ms. VD55G0 full depth is 10-bit, with RAW10 output, not 9-bit fast mode or RAW8. Autoexposure updates from preceding frame statistics; a cold first frame is not guaranteed to have converged exposure. The host must provide CLKIN before XSHUTDOWN release and wait for READY_TO_BOOT before I2C access.
findings.consequence: A steady-state 185 fps rating (~5.41 ms frame period) does not establish cold-shutter latency or image exposure quality. Long exposures and several AEC convergence frames can consume the deadline even with cut2.
findings.recommendation: Define whether the deadline means end of exposure or a complete valid frame in SRAM. Use full 644x604, normal 10-bit ADC and RAW10. Budget rail/ROM/FSBL/patch/configuration/exposure/readout separately; choose a bounded manual or seeded AEC cold-start exposure policy and record actual applied gain/exposure with the image. GPIO0 is currently unconnected, so use supported I2C follower trigger or streaming control unless precise external-trigger wiring is added.
findings.closure: Instrument power, XSHUTDOWN, MCLK, first CSI frame start/end and exposure status across light levels and supply/temperature corners.

findings.title: The 50 ms capture target needs a bounded cold-boot payload and measured startup budget
findings.observed: The design physically cold-starts and loads firmware from serial NOR before capture; the spec targets image acquisition within 50 ms. ROM uses 32 MHz single-bit data transfer, not a quad data boot.
findings.consequence: The ideal ROM data ceiling is4MB/s:100 KiB already needs 25.6 ms and 200 KiB needs 51.2 ms, before command/software/authentication overhead, rail startup, clock settling or sensor initialization. Large FSBL payloads alone can consume the complete budget. This is a quantitative risk, not a claim that every possible small FSBL fails.
findings.recommended_fix: Create a small capture-first FSBL, keep noncritical code and NAND commit after acquisition, and measure shutter-to-rails, ROM completion, first MCLK, first I2C operation and first complete frame. Coordinate sensor-revision/patch bounds in the memory/sensor review. Define whether the deadline is exposure completion or frame arrival and reserve real margin; do not infer cold-boot latency from Standby wake figures.

evidence.detail: Table14 single-line0Bh read with prescaler2; Table26 XSPI kernel from 64 MHz per_ck; no DMA for ROM SPI transfer.
Low-power wake times are not cold boot; HSE crystal startup is 2 ms typical with no guaranteed maximum.

findings.title: Directly connected capacitance and startup load need inrush control
findings.detail_markdown:
**High / measurement.** C13+C43 contribute 5.7 µF directly on VBUS. D2 also exposes approximately C1+C2=10.1 µF at SYS_IN to plug-in charging, giving roughly 15.8 µF nominal before downstream converter startup. This is more than the usual simple 10 µF input-load model. Diode drop, MLCC bias, cable resistance and soft-start affect the actual waveform, so this calculation alone is not a compliance failure measurement. U2 soft-start does not limit the initial charging of its input capacitors through D2.

**Recommendation:** Provide controlled USB input charging/current limiting and an appropriate initial operating mode. Record at least the first 100 ms at sufficient sample rate and evaluate the inrush regions using the USB-IF method. Test with empty input capacitors, weak ports, both plug orientations and battery presence/absence. Include hot-plug overshoot at U4, whose maximum operating input is 5.5 V. [USB-IF inrush test update](https://compliance.usb.org/index.asp?UpdateFile=Electrical), [TLV700 electrical limits](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tlv700.pdf#page=5).

findings.title: Debug keepout and assembly clearances need enforced rules
findings.detail_markdown:
**Medium / confirmed.** The Tag-Connect no-track/via area is drawn on Dwgs.User but has no KiCad rule-area enforcement. The switch has no courtyard. These do not alter the netlist, but a routed board can pass ordinary clearance rules while obstructing the debug probe or component assembly. U1's0.394 mm lands/paste differ slightly from the recommended0.400 mm, and the recommended0.470 mm NSMD mask opening is not explicitly encoded.

**Recommendation:** Encode the required debug exclusion area as enforceable board rules, add verified courtyards, and explicitly set the BGA copper/mask/paste geometry accepted by the assembler. Preserve the manufacturer-matched pitch, pad numbering and connector holes. The6 µm BGA land difference is a normalization/qualification item, not evidence that the current BGA cannot solder. [Critical footprint measurements and drawings](footprint-spot-check.md).

findings.title: The stated 8 V battery discharge endpoint is not enforced
findings.observed: U2 EN is tied to SYS_IN, with no battery-specific undervoltage divider/comparator. BAT_PLUS has no ADC divider; BAT_CELL1_TAP goes to RTC backup and test access rather than a cell-monitor input. The U2 power-good pins are not routed to control logic.

evidence.detail: EN=SYS_IN; PG_3V3 and PG_1V8 each have only the regulator and their pull-up resistor.
U2 falling input UVLO is2.6-2.8 V, not an8 V battery cutoff.
Reference-cell capacity is specified down to2.0 V per cell; actual selected-cell endpoint remains to be established.

findings.consequence: The converter can keep attempting operation far below the stated four-cell endpoint. Pack voltage alone also cannot distinguish one weak cell from three stronger cells. Collapse during a NAND write remains possible; a nominal 8 V assumption does not prevent it.
findings.recommendation: Define the selected-cell discharge and pulse-sag policy, then implement battery monitoring/cutoff that can act before an unsafe or unreliable capture. Consider cell imbalance and startup pulse sag when choosing thresholds. Maintain power-fail-tolerant storage behavior; regulator PG outputs currently provide no warning to firmware.

findings.title: Add observability and a production recovery path before layout
findings.detail_markdown:
**Medium / confirmed gap.** TP1–TP13 expose battery, ground, main/core/camera supplies, BOOT0, NRST, RTC bus and MCLK. They do not explicitly expose PWR_ON, both PG signals, USB input current or sensor frame timing. Both PG nets presently end at a regulator and pull-up. Many startup faults can otherwise look like an identical dead board.

**Recommendation:** Add compact accessible ground-adjacent pads for PWR_ON, power-good/sequencer states, camera shutdown and a firmware timing marker. Provide a removable current-measurement link or fixture contact for the main pack; avoid CSI branch stubs. Confirm the selected Tag-Connect cable/adaptor's pinout, mechanical access, VTref and SWO behavior, and retain recoverable boot/reset access. SW2/SW3 are inferred optional DNP additions, so their footprint and assembly variant need explicit review before fitting. Include firmware provisioning, RTC setup, device identity, known-image capture, bad-block initialization and USB download in the factory test. [Current connectivity](../../hardware/reconstruction/schematic-connectivity.json), [reconstruction decisions](../../hardware/reconstruction/reconstruction-decisions.json).

findings.title: Accelerometer cold startup consumes up to 20 ms before sampling
findings.detail_markdown:
**Medium / conditional.** U12 powers U11 from a GPIO-enabled switched rail. LIS2DW12 needs a 20 ms cold boot to load trims, followed by mode-dependent sampling/filter startup. Its much shorter single-conversion figures are not cold-power-on timing. Sequentially initializing the accelerometer and then the camera would consume avoidable latency.

**Recommendation:** Enable the accelerometer early and overlap its boot with other startup work; choose an ODR/filter mode that delivers a valid orientation sample before the image needs it. Timestamp the sample and mark invalid/transient orientation instead of silently using stale data. Provide at least 10 ms below 100 mV when a true sensor power cycle is required. Consider connecting the sensor to the main switched 1.8 V supply and using its power-down mode: the whole main supply already turns off between photographs. This removes U12/control parts but sacrifices independent isolation during long USB sessions. A gravity sensor resolves orientation relative to gravity, not absolute yaw, and motion during the shutter press can disturb that estimate. [AN5038 Rev6, pp5,10,34](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/an5038-lis2dw12-alwayson-3d-accelerometer-stmicroelectronics.pdf#page=5), [LIS2DW12 datasheet](../../datasheets/sensors_timing/LIS2DW12_datasheet.pdf).

findings.title: Keep MCU bus pins passive while the sensor rail is off
findings.detail_markdown:
**Medium / conditional.** U11 VDD/VDDIO/CS share ACCEL_1V8_SW; SA0 is grounded, selecting I2C address0x18. R30/R31=10 kΩ pull up to the switched rail, and interrupt routing uses the appropriate 1.8 V bank. These connections are consistent. U12 QOD tied to VOUT and CT left open are allowed; QOD helps discharge the sensor rail.

**Recommendation:** Disable MCU internal pull-ups and avoid driving SDA/SCL/INT high into the unpowered sensor; configure open-drain/high-impedance states before removing power. At 100 kHz, 10 kΩ pull-ups allow about 118 pF for a 1 µs RC rise limit; a short local bus is plausible, but faster operation needs its own timing check. Verify that external leakage does not defeat QOD or the required power-off interval. [LIS2DW12 electrical/I2C limits](../../datasheets/sensors_timing/LIS2DW12_datasheet.pdf), [TPS22918 QOD and CT behavior](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps22918.pdf).

findings.title: The 1.2 V camera core choice has limited tolerance margin
findings.observed: U10 NCP115AMX120TCG nominal 1.200 V supplies a sensor specified at 1.10-1.26 V, nominal 1.15 V. NCP115 specifies +/-40 mV output accuracy at its stated 1 mA test point and separately up to 30 mV load regulation for XDFN. Static 1.16-1.24 V fits, leaving only 20 mV to the sensor upper limit before accounting for other effects.
findings.consequence: The nominal value is not itself an overvoltage fault, but typical graphs or the +/-1% room-temperature headline do not establish a guaranteed rail budget across input, load, temperature and transients. Sensor core ripple allowance is 20 mV up to 10 MHz.
findings.recommendation: Close the signed worst-case regulation and transient budget using exact test conditions and actual loading. Retain U10 only if the full 1.10-1.26 V window is met at the module; otherwise select a tighter regulator nearer 1.15 V. Do not simply add all maxima as a claim of actual overvoltage.
findings.closure: Worst-case design calculation plus VCORE measurements at sensor startup/streaming, including the specified 38 mA streaming-start transient.

findings.title: XSHUTDOWN pulldown is not proven against maximum input leakage
findings.observed: R20 is 100 kohm. Sensor digital-input leakage permits 10 uA, while VIL max is 0.3*VDDIO. An adverse 10 uA leakage through 100 kohm permits 1 V, above the ~0.54 V low threshold at nominal I/O power. Actual leakage direction and MCU reset-state contributions are not characterized here.
findings.consequence: The stated default-low shutdown guarantee has no demonstrated worst-case margin during reset and rail sequencing.
findings.recommendation: Use a stronger pulldown such as 10 kohm, or document a guaranteed combined leakage bound including the MCU pin. A lower resistance adds small current only while shutdown is released. R21 U9 enable does not have this same issue: its 100 kohm with TLV700 0.5 uA maximum enable leakage yields 50 mV.
findings.closure: Guaranteed leakage calculation over corners, plus a captured reset/startup waveform below VIL until the intended release.

findings.title: Use the exact 079CLR module envelope for mechanical release
findings.observed: The existing spec used a related CAM-6G3 STEP. Exact DB5266 Rev2 specifies 079CLR head 5x5x2.8 mm, total 11.65x8x2.8 mm, and connector-to-optical-center distance 7.45 mm. ST now lists an exact CAM-5G0-079CLR STEP ZIP; direct TLS retrieval failed in this review, so no replacement model was claimed imported.
findings.consequence: Related-module geometry cannot certify flex sweep, connector orientation, optical aperture, or the complete <=5 mm product stack.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve/import the exact STEP via the listed official link or use a physical module. Combine it with the corrected J3 footprint, actual mating height, PCB/enclosure datums, clearances and optical field of view before locking placement. Evaluation-module procurement and production-unit supply should also be confirmed with the module supplier.

evidence.status: URL discovered; HTTPS client transfer reset; not locally archived

findings.closure: Exact CAD/physical fit with the intended flex orientation and a complete thickness/clearance drawing.

findings.title: The 0.81 V core label must not be treated as an 800 MHz operating point
findings.observed: The core/CSI rail is named VCORE_0V81 and the spec describes an 800 MHz MCU. The core rail is produced by the programmable internal SMPS, not a fixed external 0.81 V regulator.
findings.consequence: VOS low uses nominal 0.81 V and permits at most 600 MHz CPU;800 MHz requires VOS high, nominal 0.89 V. There is no supplied firmware proving which operating point will actually be used. A fixed 0.81 V/800 MHz configuration would be out of specification.
findings.recommended_fix: Choose the lowest operating point that meets capture timing; if using 800 MHz, program VOS high and wait for readiness before raising CPU frequency. Validate0.858-0.921 V at the core at high VOS and account for its increased transient load. Rename the rail to VDDCORE during an approved schematic revision if it will change voltage.

evidence.detail: Table 24: CPU600MHz low VOS/800 MHz high VOS; VDDCORE ranges0.782-0.842 V and0.858-0.921 V.

findings.title: Silicon revision and cold-reset recovery must be recorded before bring-up
findings.observed: The part number specifies STM32N657X0H3Q but no purchased silicon revision or ROM version is recorded. SWD pins are connected; BOOT0 and NRST pads exist, while PA6/BOOT1 only has a pull-down.
findings.consequence: ES0620 describes revision-dependent reset/boot fallbacks and all-revision clock/SMPS limitations. A stuck reset path or invalid flash state may require a real power cycle. REV_ID alone does not distinguish Z/B/X in this errata; assuming generic STM32 reset behavior would weaken recovery.
findings.recommended_fix: Record package revision marking and ROM version, apply applicable NRST and software-reset clock-mux workarounds, and avoid the internal-SMPS backup-domain reset limitation. Keep accessible SWD/NRST, BOOT0, a way to force PA6/BOOT1 development boot, and a true power-cycle path during prototype bring-up. Keep flash in a ROM-readable state before warm reset and verify production boot/recovery before locking debug or fusing boot options.

evidence.detail: Revision matrix;2.2.1 APB prescaling;2.2.5 REV_ID;2.2.12/13 FSBL fallback;2.2.15 VSWRST/SMPS;2.2.18 NRST;2.2.22 reset clocks.
Boot1 priority/development flow, no special serial-NOR setup, ROM version and diagnostics.
Boot configuration and debug management.

findings.title: Keep NAND scanning and erase work outside acquisition latency
findings.observed: The device has 2048 blocks; factory markers occupy the first spare byte of pages0 and1 in each block. At the specified 25 us maximum array-to-buffer time, a two-marker full scan can budget 4096*25 us=102.4 ms before command/transfer overhead. This is a worst-case timing budget, not a minimum or a measured scan time.
findings.consequence: An unconditional startup scan before camera capture is incompatible with a guaranteed 50 ms acquisition budget at the device timing corner, even though save completion is allowed later.
findings.recommendation: Persist redundant protected allocation/BBT checkpoints, perform first-use formatting and full recovery scans in a separate mode or after capture into SRAM, and maintain a reserve of erased good blocks. Plan recovery paths without making NAND ready a prerequisite for exposure when SRAM can hold the frame.
findings.closure: Measured normal and damaged-metadata startup paths with explicit acquisition behavior; documented minimum erased reserve.

findings.title: NOR warm-reset state needs a recovery contract
findings.observed: IQ fixes QE=1 but still accepts standard single-line SPI. WSON8 has no dedicated reset input. Guaranteed power initialization requires VCC below0.8 V for at least100 us; a processor reset or quick power re-press does not necessarily do that. UM3234 documents a fixed legacy0Bh boot read, not a documented universal flash reset/release sequence.
findings.consequence: If firmware leaves NOR in deep power-down, continuous-read/wrap state, or an unfinished write, watchdog/BOR/debug reset can re-enter ROM with an unsuitable flash state. This is conditional on firmware behavior, not a proven failure of the current absent firmware.
findings.recommendation: Keep boot NOR in a ROM-compatible state before reset and avoid deep power-down/volatile read modes unless reset recovery is demonstrated. Use the66h/99h sequence only when safe; it takes about30 us and may corrupt an active write. Respect20 us read-ready and5 ms write-inhibit after power-up. Restrict133 MHz reads to VCC>=3.0 V; at2.7 V the datasheet fast-clock limit is104 MHz.

evidence.cross_reference: MCU-001 actual boot CS error; MCU-006 ROM protocol/timing

findings.closure: Test cold, warm, watchdog, BOR, USB-powered reset and rapid re-press from every NOR state allowed by firmware.

findings.title: Narrow the first prototype's performance and operating contract
findings.detail_markdown:
**Medium / conditional.** STM32N657 provides useful native CSI and enough nominal SRAM for this image size, so replacing it is not automatically an improvement. Its cold boot, multiple power domains and large BGA add complexity that must earn their energy and latency cost. Raw NAND offers substantial capacity but adds controller/ECC and power-fail firmware work. Unspecified temperature range, cell end-of-life condition and interpretation of “capture within50 ms” prevent a single meaningful pass/fail result.

**Recommendation:** Keep the current architecture for the first measured feasibility experiment after correcting the explicit faults. Define the deadline as either exposure completion or full frame in RAM, bound exposure time, firmware load size, sensor revision and CPU operating point, and measure acquisition and commit energy separately. Run capture first with USB/NAND/background tasks deferred. Keep at least one full image plus DMA/cache/stack/firmware margin in a linker-checked SRAM plan; two unpacked 16-bit images already need about1.56 MB. Do not promise ten-year shelf life from IC typical currents or fifty-millisecond capture from isolated peripheral timings. If the corrected prototype misses the energy budget, revisit the battery and always-on/cold-start strategy before spending time on a dense final PCB. [MCU timing/operating-point findings](mcu-review.md), [camera/storage analysis](camera-memory-review.md), [power bounds](power-review.md).

findings.title: 1 MHz camera I2C needs a capacitance and pull-up budget
findings.observed: R22/R23 are 4.7 kohm to 1V8. Sensor Fm+ allows 120 ns rise time, while Fast mode allows 300 ns. A lumped RC estimate tr(30-70%)=0.8473*R*C gives maximum bus capacitance about 30 pF at 1 MHz or 75 pF at 400 kHz with these pulls.
findings.consequence: The speed used to reduce patch/configuration time is not guaranteed by choosing a 1 MHz peripheral setting; module flex, connector, MCU/sensor pads and probe capacitance all count.
findings.recommendation: Keep the bus short and measure rise/fall times at the module. Select pull-ups from actual capacitance and both devices' sink limits if Fm+ is needed. Use MCO2 on PC9 at a legal 6-27 MHz clock with the documented duty/jitter limits; MCU AF/domain checks passed separately.

evidence.section: PC9 MCO2 and PC10/PC11 I2C4 at VDDIO4=1V8

findings.closure: Scope I2C timing and MCLK at final loading; no transfer errors across supply/temperature corners.

findings.title: The 40 MHz crystal network needs startup and load qualification
findings.observed: Y1 is CX3225SA40000D0PTWCC,40 MHz,CL 8pF,ESR 50ohm maximum; C36/C37 are 8.2 pF each. ST allows16-48 MHz crystals.
findings.consequence: The first-order load estimate8.2/2+4=8.1 pF matches the requested 8 pF using ST's rough 4 pF stray estimate, so the capacitor values are not demonstrably wrong. Actual parasitics, crystal shunt capacitance, drive and startup margin remain unverified. HSERDY detects initial cycles and does not guarantee stable frequency.
findings.recommended_fix: Use C0G load capacitors and a short oscillator layout. Obtain the crystal shunt-capacitance/startup data, check critical-gm margin against the MCU 1.95 mA/V capability, and measure drive level, frequency and worst-case stable-start time across voltage/temperature. Budget that measured time before enabling USB/camera timing-critical paths.

evidence.detail: Table 49:16-48 MHz, maximum critical crystal gm 1.95 mA/V;4 pF rough combined parasitics;2 ms typical startup.
Section7.2: crystal selection and C0G load capacitors with PCB/pin capacitance.
Section2.2.24: HSERDY is not frequency-stability assurance.
Kyocera exact-MPN specification, historical TI-hosted copy:40 MHz, CL 8pF, ESR maximum 50ohm, drive maximum 200uW. Confirm current procurement specification.

findings.title: Ten-year shelf life is not established by the PFET off-state leakage limits
findings.observed: The shelf target is10+ years. The selected HUASHUO PFET permits1 uA drain leakage at25C and5 uA at55C at its specified test voltage. The series off path is not correctly modeled by adding two full IDSS limits, and actual leakage at this lower voltage may be smaller.

evidence.detail: IDSS maxima1 uA at25C and5 uA at55C, VDS=-24 V; gate leakage100 nA at|VGS|12 V.
Unselected reference capacity235 mAh and typical self-dischargeabout1% per year.
Common-source power isolation and single-cell RTC tap.

findings.consequence: Even1 uA sustained for10 years consumes87.6 mAh, about37% of the candidate235 mAh rating before captures and self-discharge. Maximum datasheet limits cannot support a10-year guarantee by themselves. The existing D3 defect must be fixed before leakage measurement is meaningful.
findings.recommendation: Set a complete off-state current budget, qualify a selected cell and isolation devices over temperature, and measure cleaned/contaminated assembled-board leakage with all interfaces absent/present as appropriate. RTC single-cell loading must be included when evaluating imbalance.

findings.title: Protection selection needs exact-vendor qualification and short return paths
findings.detail_markdown:
**Medium / measurement.** D1 is UMW USBLC6-2SC6, not the ST part with the same base name. Its connections are correct: pins1/6 DP,3/4 DM,2 ground,5 VBUS. The archived UMW sheet lists up to 1 pF I/O-to-ground capacitance and 10 V/15 V clamping at its stated 1 A/6 A tests. Those numbers alone do not prove protection of the MCU under an assembled-product ESD event.

**Recommendation:** Route connector → protection → PHY without protection stubs; give the clamp and shield a short, low-inductance ground return. Select an exact traceable device with adequate characterization, then validate USB signal quality and the intended ESD test level. Consider VBUS transient/overvoltage protection as part of the input switch selection. CC pins presently terminate only through Rd, so an MCU CC-pin overvoltage fault is not claimed here. SBU pins being unused and shield tabs being grounded are reasonable for this USB2 sink. [Archived exact-vendor UMW datasheet](../../datasheets/discretes/UMW_USBLC6-2SC6_datasheet.pdf), [GCT connector drawing](../../datasheets/connectors/USB4105_drawing.pdf).

findings.title: AC remains supported; AD substitution changes the storage format
findings.observed: Macronix March2026 MPLP lists MX30LF2G18AC-TI as recommended for new design with longevity support throughDec2029; AD-TI is listed throughJul2030. This is not an EOL notice. The migration note changes AC4-bit/528B and64-byte spare to AD8-bit/544B and128-byte spare, with different endurance and program/erase performance.
findings.consequence: There is no evidence here requiring an immediate AC replacement. A purchasing substitution to AD without firmware/format qualification would be unsafe, and longevity horizon should be checked against the intended production period.
findings.recommendation: Keep exact MPN control, confirm supply/support horizon directly with Macronix, and qualify AD as a separate device/format if desired. Do not label AC obsolete from distributor stock or the existence of a migration note.
findings.closure: Supplier lifecycle confirmation and a controlled alternate-device qualification before substitutions.

findings.title: Resolve the optional pull-down and interrupt voltage before release
findings.detail_markdown: **Low / confirmed, with the high-severity voltage issue tracked as MCU-004.** R26=1 MΩ is fitted on RTC SDA although source prose calls it optional/DNP. It draws about 3.3 µA while the main-powered bus is high; it is not a ten-year backup drain because the pull-up rail is off and the RTC bus is high impedance during backup. Choose fitted/DNP intentionally. R25=10 kΩ correctly defines EVI low; CLKOUT is explicitly unused. R28/R29=4.7 kΩ are plausible local bus pull-ups, subject to measured rise time. U8's interrupt is open drain, so changing R24's pull-up to the receiving 1.8 V domain is preferable to adding a translator. [RV-3028 manual pp45,94–97](../../datasheets/sensors_timing/RV-3028-C8_application_manual.pdf); physical nets in [schematic-connectivity.json](../../hardware/reconstruction/schematic-connectivity.json).

findings.title: Qualify the clear-filter optics for intended lighting
findings.observed: The selected 079CLR has a clear filter and 13.5 cm-to-infinity depth of field. ST AN5836 documents persistent visible-domain artifacts after intense focused illumination, including when the sensor is unpowered.
findings.consequence: A powered-off outdoor camera can still acquire image artifacts; close-up behavior and spectral appearance are also properties of the selected optical module, not MCU processing.
findings.recommendation: Include intended outdoor/indoor lighting and near-distance scenes in optical qualification. If necessary, add an optical cover/shutter or revise the filter/module specification with the supplier; avoid treating power gating as optical protection.
findings.closure: Acceptable images after intended storage/illumination exposure and at required scene distances.
